You are an expert in analyzing logs of test execution script and dockerfile construction.  
Your task is to verify whether the target tests have been executed correctly and, if not, diagnose the issues.
Background: To run the target test files of a given repository, we create a Dockerfile and an eval script. We plan to invoke the eval script inside the container built by that Dockerfile.

You will:
1. Analyze the log of test execution to check if the target tests were executed and whether they passed.
2. If the tests did not run correctly, determine whether the issue is related to:
   - The **Dockerfile** (environment setup issues)
   - The **evaluation script** (test execution issues)
   - Missing information that needs to be collected

3. Based on your analysis, provide **clear guidance** to the appropriate agent:
   - `write_dockerfile_agent`
   - `write_eval_script_agent`
   - `context_retrieval_agent`

Your findings and recommendations must be structured in a JSON format, ensuring efficient collaboration with other agents.

The current dockerfile used to setup environemnt:
# Use Ubuntu 22.04 without platform override to avoid extraction errors related to platform specifier
FROM ubuntu:22.04
ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV TZ=Etc/UTC

# Install essential system dependencies, git, curl, wget, python3.10 and build tools
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    software-properties-common \
    && add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa -y \
    && apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    git \
    wget \
    curl \
    build-essential \
    python3.10 \
    python3.10-venv \
    python3.10-distutils \
    python3-pip \
    python3-setuptools \
    python3.10-dev \
    locales \
    locales-all \
    tzdata \
    bash \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set default python alternative to python3.10
RUN update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python3 python3 /usr/bin/python3.10 1

# Set locale to UTF-8 to avoid locale-related warnings
RUN locale-gen en_US.UTF-8
ENV LANG=en_US.UTF-8
ENV LANGUAGE=en_US:en
ENV LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8

# Create necessary directory structure and set permissions for Poetry installation
RUN mkdir -p /root/.local/share/pypoetry && \
    chown -R root:root /root/.local

# Download Poetry installation script separately and explicitly run it to better handle errors and layer snapshot issues
RUN curl -sSL https://install.python-poetry.org -o install-poetry.py && \
    python3 install-poetry.py --version 1.9.6 && \
    rm install-poetry.py

ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Verify poetry installation by printing version (fail early if install failed)
RUN poetry --version

# Clone the repository, checkout the given commit
WORKDIR /testbed/
RUN git clone https://github.com/AntonOsika/gpt-engineer.git /testbed && \
    git reset --hard 3e589bf1356024fb471a9d17738e4626f21a953b

# Configure Poetry to create virtual env inside project, install dependencies, then install package in editable mode
RUN poetry config virtualenvs.create true && \
    poetry config virtualenvs.in-project true && \
    poetry install --no-root --only main,dev

RUN /bin/bash -c "source /testbed/.venv/bin/activate && pip install -e ."

# Set default shell as bash
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]

# Default workdir
WORKDIR /testbed/

# Expose HOME environment to ensure Poetry and virtual env works smoothly
ENV HOME=/root

# Provide a bashrc line to activate poetry shell (virtual env) automatically for convenience during interactive use
RUN echo "source /testbed/.venv/bin/activate" >> /root/.bashrc

The current eval script (omit test patch to decrease length) used to run tests:
#!/bin/bash
set -uxo pipefail

cd /testbed
git checkout 3e589bf1356024fb471a9d17738e4626f21a953b

# Apply the test patch
git apply -v - <<'EOF_114329324912'
[CONTENT OF TEST PATCH]
EOF_114329324912

# Activate poetry virtual environment and run the specific test file with pytest
# We show file name, result summary and avoid unrelated verbosity
source /testbed/.venv/bin/activate

poetry run pytest --no-header -rA --tb=short tests/test_azure_deployment_name.py

rc=$?

echo "OMNIGRIL_EXIT_CODE=$rc"

# Revert patch after test run to clean workspace
git checkout 3e589bf1356024fb471a9d17738e4626f21a953b tests/test_azure_deployment_name.py
